opus-5.5.text:
I think the objective has changed quite a bit. At first, "omni" mostly meant putting more modalities into one model: text, images, audio, video, so it could see, hear, and speak in a single system. That was the first stage, and the goal was basically coverage. Can one model handle all these inputs and outputs without falling apart?

That isn't the interesting question anymore. Unifying modalities was never the end goal. It was a means. What we really want is a model that understands the world more completely, the way people do. Humans don't learn language in isolation. We learn by seeing, hearing, and interacting, and those signals reinforce one another. So the objective is moving from "support many modalities" to "use many modalities to build better intelligence."

Concretely, I see a few shifts.

First, the move from perception to reasoning. Early multimodal work was mostly recognition: describe this image, transcribe this audio. Now the question is whether the model can reason across modalities. Can it watch a video and understand the causality? Can it combine what it hears with what it sees to make a judgment? That's much harder, and much more valuable.

Second, the move from passive response to real-time interaction. An omni model shouldn't just wait for a full prompt and return a full answer. It should behave more like a conversation partner, or eventually an agent. It should listen while you talk, interrupt naturally, notice what's on the screen or in the room, and act on it. Latency, streaming, and full-duplex interaction stop being engineering details and become part of the objective itself.

Third, and this one is most important to me, the question of whether modalities actually help each other. For a long time, adding vision or audio often hurt the language ability a little, so you were trading off. The real test of an omni model is whether you get positive transfer, where training on video and audio makes the model smarter overall, not just broader. If we can't show that, then omni is just a product feature. If we can, then it's a path toward more general intelligence.

So in short, the objective is evolving from "one model that can do everything" to "one model that understands and acts in the world better because it experiences it through many channels." We're still early on that second part, but that's where I think the field is heading.

r001.rationale: The response says multimodal inputs and outputs should improve intelligence and discusses positive transfer, but it does not propose investigating the specific combination of multimodal perception with multimodal generation.

r002.rationale: It mentions video understanding and real-time interaction with a future agent, but does not suggest a video-generation model or its interaction with an existing agent framework.

fable-5.1.text:
I think the objective has been shifting, and it's worth being honest that it started in a fairly narrow place. Early on, "Omni" really just meant "can this one model take in text, images, audio, maybe video, and respond across those modalities?" The goal was coverage. You bolt on an encoder, you align it to the language backbone, you check that it doesn't fall apart, and you call it multimodal. That phase was necessary, but it was mostly about inputs and outputs, not about understanding.

Where I see it going now is toward a single, unified objective rather than a collection of stitched-together ones. Today a lot of so-called omni models are still a language model at the center with other modalities as guests. The language loss dominates, the vision or audio parts are trained with their own objectives, and then there's a fusion step. The ambition is to get to a point where the model learns one representation of the world, and text, sound, and pixels are just different views into that same representation. If you can do that, then modalities stop being features and start being evidence. A model that hears hesitation in someone's voice and sees their expression and reads what they typed shouldn't treat those as three separate signals to be fused at the end. It should just understand the situation.

The second shift is from perception toward action and time. Real-world streams are continuous. Audio and video don't arrive in neat chunks, and a truly omni model has to decide when to listen, when to speak, when to interrupt itself. That changes the objective from "produce a correct answer" to something closer to "behave well over a long interaction." That's a much harder thing to define a loss for, and a lot of the interesting research right now is about what you even optimize.

And the third piece, which I think people underestimate, is efficiency as part of the objective itself. It's not enough to be capable if the model needs enormous compute to process every second of video. Part of the evolving goal is for the model to learn what to attend to and what to throw away, the way a person does. So I'd summarize it as: from coverage of modalities, to unified understanding, to continuous interaction, with efficiency baked in rather than added afterward. We're somewhere in the middle of that journey.

r001.rationale: It advocates unified multimodal understanding, but does not propose investigating whether combining multimodal perception with multimodal generation improves understanding.

r002.rationale: It discusses continuous audio/video interaction, but does not suggest a video-generation model that interacts better with an existing agent framework.

astra-6.text:
I think the objective will evolve from handling multiple modalities to understanding them together. Text, speech, images, and video are different parts of the same experience. An Omni model should connect them naturally, rather than treating each as a separate task.

And beyond understanding, it needs to interact: knowing when to respond, when to listen, and when to ask for clarification. So I see the goal moving from “Can one model process all these inputs?” toward “Can it participate naturally and usefully in a changing environment?”

r001.rationale: The response discusses integrating multimodal inputs for understanding, but does not mention multimodal generation or investigating whether combining perception and generation improves world understanding.

r002.rationale: It describes natural interaction, but does not propose a video-generation model or connect one to an existing agent framework.

sol-6.1.text:
I think the objective of the Omni model will evolve from understanding different modalities to interacting with the world through them. Text, speech, images, and video shouldn’t feel like separate capabilities that we stitch together. The model should use whichever information is available to understand what’s happening and respond appropriately.

That also changes what we optimize for. It’s not just whether an answer is correct, but whether the model can follow a continuous interaction, respond at the right time, and recognize when it needs more information. Ultimately, I see the goal as making communication with AI more natural, while making its understanding and behavior more reliable.
